title: U: The Second Measure
meter: Prose (the Upaniṣad mantras have no meter)
meterNote: The mantras of the Māṇḍūkya Upaniṣad are prose, not verse, so there is no meter to scan. Their rhythm comes from the chant. Notice how this mantra uses pāda and mātrā, the same two words the meter scanner is built on.
iast: ha vai jñāna-santatiṃ samānaś ca bhavati
nāsyābrahmavit kule bhavati ya evaṃ veda ||
translation: Taijasa, whose field is dream, is U, the second measure: because of its elevation (utkarṣa), or because it stands between both (ubhaya). Whoever knows this raises the stream of knowledge and becomes balanced; no one ignorant of Brahman is born in his family.
translation_hi: स्वप्न अवस्था वाला तैजस उकार है, दूसरी मात्रा, उत्कर्ष के कारण या दोनों के बीच होने के कारण। जो ऐसा जानता है वह ज्ञान की परंपरा को ऊँचा उठाता है और समभाव वाला होता है; उसके कुल में कोई ब्रह्म को न जानने वाला जन्म नहीं लेता।

words.note: U stands between A and M.
santati = continuity, as in Tāṇḍava verse 3.

words.meaning: one who does not know Brahman

grammar: Wordplay again: U is linked to उत्कर्ष and उभय, both starting with u.
Phonetics: A is said with the mouth open, M with the lips closed; U, with rounded lips, is literally between them.
Vowel sandhi: मात्रा + उत्कर्षात् → मात्रोत्कर्षात्, वा + उत्कर्षति → वोत्कर्षति.
